source.title: Unraveling the Enigma of Double Descent: An In-depth Analysis through the Lens of Learned Feature Space
source.authors: Yu-Fei Gu; Xiao-Qing Zheng; T. Aste

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper says it replicates the model-wise double-descent experiment framework of Nakkiran et al. and sweeps model width while measuring test error on neural networks.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses epoch-wise and sample-wise double descent in its related-work section but cites prior work rather than testing those versions. Its k-NN analyses of noisy training examples are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study replicates Nakkiran et al.'s model-wise width sweeps (FCNN on MNIST, 5-layer CNN and ResNet18 on CIFAR-10) and reports test-error curves at several explicit label-noise levels. This bears on V1, and on the noise-dependence part of V6. It is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with two additions. The authors argue that double descent arises only in imperfect learners trained on noisy data: error first rises with classical overfitting, then extra parameters let the model isolate noise. They conjecture, without testing it, that a perfect learner with optimal regularization shows no peak. They concede the ResNet18 feature-space result contradicts their isolation hypothesis, and that a full theoretical account is still missing.
record.recipe_differences: The study says it replicates Nakkiran et al.'s experimental framework, using width sweeps and test-error measurements on FCNNs, CNNs, and ResNet18s. It adds explicit label-noise comparisons and a k-NN learned-feature-space analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error shape varies with dataset, architecture, and label-noise level: the MNIST FCNN at p = 0% is monotone, while the noisy MNIST FCNN and the reported CIFAR-10 models show double descent. The paper also says the peak grows as label noise increases.

fits_no_version.finding: k-NN (cosine similarity, penultimate layer) accuracy P for noisy training points tracks test accuracy for FCNN and CNN. For ResNet18, P on clean labels drops to zero at the interpolation threshold, which the authors say contradicts their isolation hypothesis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-parameterized networks place mislabeled training points among clean points of their true class in feature space, and this tracks the second descent (architecture-dependent).

record.problems: The reported curves are primarily presented in figures without extracted numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The number of repeated runs is not stated. The experiments cover selected image datasets and architectures, and do not test epoch-wise or sample-wise double descent. The paper itself notes that its k-NN method is only an estimation technique and that its interpretation is limited by feature-space complexity.

untested.parts: Only width sweeps on FCNN/MNIST (N=4000) and CNN/ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 were run, without data augmentation or regularization. No other architectures, depths or datasets were tested.

Triple or multiple descent was not tested. Whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak is only conjectured in the conclusion and the Figure 4 schematic, not tested. Variance from sources other than labels was not studied.
Not tested: no test-error-over-epochs curves are reported.
Not tested: training-set size is fixed.
Not tested: only neural networks are studied.
Not tested: no effective-complexity measure is evaluated.
Not tested: the x-axis is width k, and the paper only notes width is monotone in parameter count.

missing.what: For CNNs, label noise shifts the interpolation threshold, and with it the test-error peak, toward larger widths.
With added noise, over-parameterized CNNs beat ResNet18s by about 5% in test accuracy, though ResNets are better at intermediate widths.

record.verdict_notes: All results are figure-only, with no numbers or error bars. Runs are 'replicated multiple times', but the count is not given. Training lengths differ: 4000 epochs for FCNN, 200 for CNN and ResNet. No regularization or augmentation is used, so the V6 regularization clause cannot be tested. The record's V6 label cited r1 without linking it; this is fixed above. The V6 support rests on FCNN and CNN only.

versions.untested_parts: The tested settings are the stated architecture, dataset, and label-noise combinations; other architectures, datasets, and training setups are not tested.
No test-error curve over training epochs is reported.
The experiments test neural networks, not a range of model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated as predicting peak locations across size, epochs, or samples.

The paper varies explicit label-noise levels and reports how the test-error peak changes. It does not test triple or multiple descent, or experimentally test whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
The paper does not recast complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that changes the curve into an ordinary U shape.
